## Line 302

```plato

    //==
    // # Warm starting
    //
    // Collision detection runs afresh every frame and hands the solver rows whose
    // accumulated impulses are zero. Starting from zero every frame is what makes a
    // stack of boxes sink into itself: the solver spends its whole iteration budget
    // rediscovering the support impulses it already found last frame, and never
    // gets past that.
    //
    // Warm starting copies the previous frame's accumulated impulses onto the rows
    // describing the same contact — same ordered body pair, contact point within a
    // tolerance — so the solver starts from last frame's answer and spends its
    // budget on the difference. It is the single highest-value step in a contact
    // solver, and here it is only field copying.
    //
    // The match is a linear scan per fresh row, so the cost is the product of the
    // two contact counts. A production engine keeps a persistent manifold keyed by
    // shape-feature ids and pays nothing; that bookkeeping needs a contact to have
    // an identity, which this vocabulary deliberately does not give it.

    // True when two rows describe the same contact: the same ordered body pair, and
    // contact points within `tolerance` of each other.
    SameContact(a: ContactConstraint3D, b: ContactConstraint3D, tolerance: Length): Boolean
        => a.BodyA.Value == b.BodyA.Value
        && a.BodyB.Value == b.BodyB.Value
        && a.Point.DistanceSquared(b.Point) <= tolerance.Amount * tolerance.Amount;
```
